ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance and continuous screening against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) PRC MOFA/MOFCOM anti-sanctions and unreliable-entity lists; (iii) Taiwan FSC terrorist-financing and sanctions designations; (iv) OFAC SDN, Consolidated, and sectoral lists with FinCEN advisories, compulsory because the gateway clears over Visa/Mastercard Direct and Fedwire rails. PEP classification covers PRC and Taiwan public officials, senior political figures, and family members; any PEP or sanctioned-category hit triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD), source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and senior-management sign-off under FATF Recommendations 10-12, the PRC AML Law (2024), and Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act Article 7.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MOEA Company Registration and Commerce Administration Services Portal (經濟部全國商工行政服務入口網, https://gcis.nat.gov.tw); company name and business-scope pre-investigation module (公司名稱及所營事業預查).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters and must end with the entity-type suffix 有限公司 (Limited Company) for the JV. The MOEA pre-investigation system matches phonetically and by character against existing and reserved names. An English or romanized name may be filed only as a secondary appellation and does not displace the Chinese legal name. For internationally branded payment products, a transliteration or descriptive English name may be notified to the MOEA, but all FSC licensing and card-scheme filings must use the registered Chinese name together with a certified English translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 銀行 (Bank) - requires prior FSC banking license
保險 (Insurance) - requires FSC insurance license
證券 (Securities) - requires FSC securities license
支付 (Payment) / 電子支付 (Electronic Payment) - requires FSC license under the Payment Services Act 2024
中華民國 (Republic of China attribution) - prohibited in private company names
Government or official sponsorship tokens implying state endorsement
國際 (International) - requires demonstrated bona fide cross-border operations
台灣 / 臺灣 (Taiwan) - restricted and conditioned by MOEA guidelines for mainland-invested companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is valid for 180 days and may be extended once for an additional 180 days by filing before expiry. On rejection, the applicant may (1) apply for administrative re-examination within 15 days of the rejection notice; (2) file an administrative appeal with the MOEA Administrative Appeal Committee (訴願審議委員會) within 30 days of notification under the Administrative Appeal Act; and (3) initiate judicial review at the Taipei High Administrative Court within 2 months of an unsuccessful appeal. As a parallel measure, the applicant may immediately resubmit a modified company name while the appeal is pending to protect the incorporation timetable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for license activation. The FSC requires the JV to maintain a substantive physical office in Taiwan with dedicated compliance, audit, and operations premises; a virtual-office address cannot satisfy the registered-office and business-substance requirements under the Taiwan Company Act and the Payment Services Act for a high-risk PSP. A serviced office may be used only during the pre-licensing setup phase (maximum 6 months), not as the final registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - estimated 70% likelihood of at least one unannounced FSC on-site inspection within the first 12 months of license activation; combined MOEA Investment Commission and Central Bank monitoring raises the joint inspection probability to approximately 75-80%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法) Articles 128–156 (incorporation and share structure of a company limited by shares), Articles 387–398 (company registration); Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例) Articles 1–14 (foreign investment screening and approval); Electronic Payment Institution Act (電子支付機構管理條例) Article 8 (paid-in capital floor and FSC licensing preconditions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan), Department of Commerce — Company Registration Division (經濟部商業發展署公司登記組), Taipei regional commercial registration office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) submitted through the MOEA Company Registration Online One-Stop System (公司登記一站式線上申請網站).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a company limited by shares under the Company Act (the former NT$1,000,000 floor was repealed); however, the FSC imposes a separate, materially higher paid-in capital floor at the electronic-payment licensing stage. For incorporation, the subscribed capital must be deposited into a Taiwan-dollar or foreign-currency escrow account opened in the JV's name, verified by a licensed CPA, and the funds remain escrowed (non-withdrawable) until the MOEA issues the incorporation registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under the Taiwan Company Act is ratified, and the subscription and allotment of shares to the founding shareholders per the Articles of Incorporation are approved. The paid-in capital shall be remitted to the Company's escrow account with a licensed bank in Taiwan.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [Taipei City address] as the Company's statutory seat for service of process.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Chairperson, [Name] a Director, and [Name] General Manager, each serving until the next general meeting.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairperson shall execute incorporation filings, open bank accounts, appoint the CPA for capital verification, and complete all registrations with the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance of Taiwan (R.O.C.), administered operationally through the relevant National Taxation Bureau; primary portals include the Ministry of Finance eTax Portal and the Ministry of Economic Affairs Company and Business One-Stop Service system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Taiwan-incorporated Sino-foreign equity joint venture must first complete company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the competent local authority, obtain its Unified Business Number (UBN), and register its business tax status with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing taxable business. The UBN generally serves as the enterprise tax identification number and business tax registration number. The application package ordinarily includes the articles of incorporation, company registration approval, foreign investor approval and investment documents where applicable, registered office evidence, responsible-person identification, capital verification or bank evidence where required, business-scope details, and banking information. A foreign company operating through a Taiwan branch follows branch-registration and tax-registration procedures. A nonresident foreign electronic-services provider supplying Taiwan consumers may require separate business tax registration under the foreign electronic-services rules, subject to the applicable sales threshold and transaction characterization. A payment-service provider must separately obtain the required Financial Supervisory Commission authorization or license before conducting regulated payment, acquiring, clearing, remittance, or electronic-payment activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a United States-style check-the-box election for companies. A Taiwan company is generally taxed as a separate legal person on Taiwan-source income and other income within the applicable corporate income tax regime. A foreign enterprise may operate through a subsidiary or branch, but the choice is structural rather than an elective tax classification. Partnerships and other pass-through arrangements may receive entity-specific treatment, but a limited company or equity joint venture is not generally permitted to elect pass-through treatment. No general hybrid-mismatch election permits a company to change from entity-level taxation to transparent taxation. Treaty relief, withholding-tax reductions, approved investment incentives, and qualifying industry incentives are claim-based statutory mechanisms, not entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Business Tax, principally implemented through Value-Added Tax (VAT).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold permits a Taiwan-incorporated company conducting taxable business to avoid business-tax registration; registration is required before commencement of business. The commonly referenced NT$40,000 monthly threshold concerns certain small-scale businesses and tax-assessment treatment and is not a general exemption from registration for a corporate payment-service provider. Foreign electronic-service providers supplying Taiwan consumers may be subject to a separate NT$600,000 annual sales threshold under the applicable electronic-services business-tax rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan businesses subject to business tax generally must issue government-regulated electronic invoices where required by the applicable e-invoice rules and transmit invoice information through the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Platform or an approved service provider. Required invoice data must use prescribed formats, authentication, numbering, buyer information, tax amounts, and cancellation or allowance procedures. Taiwan does not generally operate a universal real-time VAT clearance model for every invoice; transmission timing depends on the invoice category and applicable regulations. Digital certificates, API or batch-upload connectivity, invoice archival, and electronic-accounting controls may be required. Payment-service providers must also maintain transaction, settlement, customer-identification, and audit records under financial-supervision and anti-money-laundering rules. Payment processing, acquiring, clearing, platform, and financial-intermediation fees must be classified transaction by transaction because particular financial services may be exempt or subject to special business-tax treatment, while ordinary taxable service fees generally bear 5% VAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated business tax may apply to qualifying exported goods and qualifying services supplied to foreign customers and used outside Taiwan, subject to the Business Tax Act and implementing rules. For a cross-border payment gateway, zero rating is not automatic merely because the customer, settlement bank, or payment rail is outside Taiwan. The taxpayer must establish that the contractual recipient is a foreign customer, the service is exported or utilized outside Taiwan, the transaction is not actually used in Taiwan, and the service is not an exempt financial service or another specially regulated category. Supporting evidence should include contracts, service descriptions, merchant and customer location data, transaction and settlement records, invoices, foreign-currency receipt evidence, bank statements, remittance records, fee calculations, and documentation demonstrating offshore utilization. Zero-rated input business tax may generally be refundable or creditable when the statutory export conditions and documentary requirements are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, where goods are exported
Commercial invoice and packing list, where goods are exported
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or equivalent transport evidence, where goods are exported
Foreign customer contract, purchase order, or service agreement
Tax invoices or e-invoices identifying the zero-rated supply
Foreign-exchange receipt, bank remittance advice, or equivalent payment evidence
Settlement and transaction reports proving the offshore service recipient, payment flow, and service utilization
Evidence of customs export clearance or other proof of export for goods
Accounting records reconciling declared export turnover, received consideration, and claimed input-tax refunds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export proceeds and qualifying offshore-service receipts are generally subject to Taiwan foreign-exchange declaration and settlement requirements, commonly requiring repatriation or settlement within six months, subject to permitted exceptions, approved extensions, transaction structure, and Central Bank rules. A taxpayer claiming zero rating without proving export status, foreign customer status, offshore utilization, or receipt of consideration may have the zero-rated treatment denied, with the applicable 5% business tax assessed retroactively, together with interest, late-payment charges, and related penalties. Improper input-tax refunds may be clawed back. Business Tax Act violations may result in administrative penalties that can be calculated by reference to the tax evaded, including substantial multiples in cases of tax evasion, false invoicing, omitted sales, or fraudulent refund claims. Serious falsification, concealment, forged documentation, or deliberate evasion may create criminal exposure for responsible persons and involved agents. Financial-sector licensing breaches, AML failures, unauthorized payment activity, and inaccurate regulatory reporting may separately trigger Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions, license restrictions, disgorgement, or criminal liability.

stage_4.bank_name: Bank of China (中国银行股份有限公司)
stage_4.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / FDI Capital Fund (资本金账户) and Operational Account (基本存款账户)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Act and Recognized Financial Statements (Company Act Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Administration Office; local municipality commercial registration authority in Taipei, New Taipei or Taoyuan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company no later than 30 June of the following year; a 30-day extension may be obtained with competent authority approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company representatives may be fined NT$10,000–NT$50,000 per Company Act Article 170 and related enforcement rules; continued non-compliance can trigger a compulsory dissolution order and administrative deregistration of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Corporate Income Tax Settlement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (jurisdictional branch based on company domicile)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following taxable year; extended to 30 June for taxpayers adopting electronic filing where so prescribed by the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent filing exposes the company to surcharges computed on underpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest at the postal savings rate; deliberate non-filing or fraudulent underreporting may result in penalties up to 100% of the under-assessed tax and compulsory collection action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Electronic Payment Institution Annual Business and Financial Compliance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Banking Bureau – Electronic Payment and Payment Systems Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (by 31 March of the following year) or such later date as specified in the electronic payment license conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of the Electronic Payment Institutions Act or license conditions may lead to corrective orders and fines from NT$500,000 to NT$10 million; serious or repeat violations can result in suspension or revocation of the PSP license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance Return and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) AML/CFT Supervisory Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: As instructed by the FSC, typically no later than 30 June following the close of the report year; exact date set by annual FSC circular
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the Money Laundering Control Act and associated regulations exposes the licensee to administrative fines up to NT$2,000,000 plus corrective requirements; egregious or repeated AML failures may lead to license revocation and compulsory strike-off of the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit required if the company is: (i) a public company; (ii) a non-public company with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million; (iii) a licensed electronic payment institution or financial institution; or (iv) expressly designated by the central competent authority under Company Act Article 20.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies adopt Taiwan IFRS as endorsed by the FSC; non-public companies apply the Commercial Accounting Act and the Regulations on the Preparation of Financial Reports, which are broadly IFRS-aligned. Cross-border payment gateway activities must additionally follow FSC accounting, audit, and transaction record-keeping requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a standalone annual UBO filing for an unlisted JV; however, the licensed electronic payment institution must verify and maintain beneficial ownership records under the Money Laundering Control Act and update these records upon any triggering event. Any transfer representing 10% or more of shares in the licensed entity must be reported to the FSC before completion, and the annual AML/CFT return must confirm the current beneficial ownership structure. The company secretary must also update the share transfer ledger before the annual general meeting and present the shareholder register for inspection before each dividend record date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share Transfer Ledger and Stock Certificate Issuance Record
Retained Financial Statements and CPA Audit Reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 - US$12,000 per annum for an SME PSP with cross-border transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory across-the-board tax holiday is granted to payment gateways; a qualifying enterprise may utilise an incremental R&D tax credit of up to 15% under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, an additional 15% credit for expenditures on 'smart machinery' or '5+2' industrial innovation, and a 5% retained-earnings surcharge applies on undistributed surplus under Article 66-9 if profits are not distributed in the following year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 15 (營利事業所得稅結算申報書) filed via the Taiwan Ministry of Finance Tax Filing Portal (電子申報繳稅服務網站); authentication through Government Service Network certificate or appointed tax filing agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual filing and final payment are due within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year; calendar-year filers must file between 1 May and 31 May of the following year. Provisional tax is due 30 September of the current fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name in Chinese and English, Unified Business Number, tax file number, fiscal year and closing date, and the ISIC/sector code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete with the Taiwan-resident JV names only; non-resident shareholders must be recorded in the shareholding annex but are not entered in the header.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue: merchant acquiring fees, gateway service fees, settlement commissions, foreign-exchange spread and ancillary revenue from payment processing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a mainland China parent provides settlement services and receives fees separately, those fees are not reported as the JV's revenue unless the JV operates as a principal; amounts collected on behalf of non-resident merchants are not gross revenue of the JV unless a processing fee is earned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cost of processing services: card scheme interchange, acquiring bank charges, clearing/network fees, chargeback and fraud losses, and security compliance expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident acquiring banks and parent-affiliate processors must satisfy the arm's length test; foreign service invoices must be retained and Taiwan withholding tax must be effected on chargeable payments to non-resident parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before loss offset; apply permitted loss carryforward and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Taiwan-resident JV, worldwide taxable income is declared; foreign-source income of the non-resident shareholder is not included; a Chinese parent with a Taiwan permanent establishment must attribute only PE income to Line 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All controlled transactions with related parties, including management fees, royalty payments, interest, and acquisition fees, with functions and risk analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related parties must make available local/master file and accounting evidence; the Taiwanese entity must ensure TP documentation is prepared before the annual filing deadline to avoid penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual return: surcharge of 3% of assessed tax for each two-month period, capped at 10%; underpayment from misdeclaration: penalty up to three times the underpaid tax; criminal liable persons face imprisonment up to five years; overdue tax arrears after final assessment result in mandatory interest and exit-control orders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on gross cash or scrip dividends to non-resident corporate shareholders; 21% to non-resident individual shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File a 'Tax Agreement Relief Application for Withholding Tax' with the National Taxation Bureau before the distribution date, attaching a Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial ownership declaration. The prescribed certificate must be issued by the treaty partner's tax authority within the prior year. An approved lower rate applies at source; otherwise the excess may be claimed by refund within five years. In respect of mainland China, the signed Cross-Strait Tax Agreement lacks active implementation and is not currently available to reduce the 20% statutory WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statute: 20% WHT on royalties and 20% WHT on debt interest paid to non-resident profit-seeking enterprises. Effective DTAs generally cap both at 10% for beneficial owners, subject to the same TRC approval protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$200 million in annual controlled related-party transactions combined with NT$300 million revenue triggers the Local File; a Master File is additionally necessary where the global ultimate parent has consolidated revenue in excess of NT$10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not maintain a separate Economic Substances Regulation regime; nevertheless, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Tax Collection Act Article 12-1) empowers the NTA to recharacterise a JV lacking genuine office, personnel, control and risk-taking as a conduit. In such circumstances the JV can be treated as a non-resident's permanent establishment, and the entire Taiwan-source income is subject to 20% corporate tax and WHT, with penalties.
